scope: Actual bridge/UI functions with bounded synthetic API; no native gameplay assertion
checks: Partial builder loss prunes job, journal and dead FIFO keys together without recruiting anyone
All builders lost retains both foundation and future blueprint as Waiting for trucks with one group Resume
Explicit replacement resumes exact existing foundation then the original next job, retaining progress and normal build orders
A living assigned truck en route to an existing foundation shows Trucks en route; later FIFO sites stay Queued, and last-worker loss shows Waiting for trucks
FIFO status follows actual worker queues even when a recovered foundation was adopted after older queued plans
A selected group keeps its existing FIFO ahead of resumed work; other original sessions are excluded
No selection, changed/foreign/non-constructor IDs, duplicates, stale context/time and unreachable groups issue no orders
A changed exact group, reordered IDs, missing jobs and completed/deleted bound targets cannot be resurrected
Orphan native foundations recover by exact owned target and ordinary HELPBUILD, without new building costs
Legacy observer-only plans disappear when their native worker queue dies; a real unfinished legacy foundation remains resumable
Two factory module levels remain serialized; an unfinished current level receives HELPBUILD before the next module is built
Native-only interrupted module recovery helps the exact current module instead of purchasing the next level
STOP/manual movement cancels only affected assigned FIFOs and preserves unrelated orphan plans; cancel remains real native STOP
A canceled unstarted journal cannot steal the later real foundation or obscure its live progress
Legacy loaded lost jobs infer identity from the retained journal, retain original plans through JSON save, and revoke stale recovery context
UI Resume obtains fresh explicit constructor IDs, never a stale build group; pending STOP cancels the unsent action
Campaign policy and frozen generated Campaign source/data remain untouched
